quote: My son, even my son that was here looking, but they were gonna send it to me. They went online. They got with the company they wanted to go with, and they already picked one.
stewart_read: This is the first and clearest disclosure that the son researched and selected a competitor online — real competitive intelligence (which company, what they saw) that the rep never asks about. This predates and is more specific than the later utility-account mention.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be deliberately not derailing into competitor detail to keep the call 'super quick' as promised at 00:22 — but even a 5-second probe ('who'd you go with?') would have armed the closer without lengthening the call meaningfully.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask one quick follow-up when a competitor is mentioned — company name and what was shown — so the closer isn't walking in blind.

quote: we'd love to just kinda show you our design here and, you know, just in case we could offer you a better system or better price.
stewart_read: This is a reasonable strategy-match to the signed_with_someone rebuttal (validation/comparison framing) — the rep doesn't argue or concede, he offers to compare. It's soft in delivery (heavy hedging: 'kinda,' 'just in case') but the underlying move is correct.
coaching_implication: The strategy is right; the delivery could be tightened — fewer hedge words would make the offer sound more confident and less apologetic.

quote: Yeah. Because he's the one everything is in his name as for utilities right now.
stewart_read: Customer states the son holds the utility account and, per the 00:39 disclosure, is the one who picked the competitor — this is squarely the adult_child_decision_maker protocol trigger. Rep says 'Gotcha' and moves straight to scheduling without looping the son in.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is more supported here: the rep had a clean opening to say 'let's get your son on this call too' per the protocol template and simply didn't take it.
coaching_implication: This is the priority coaching moment — walk the rep through the protocol template and show how a same-day or evening appointment could include the son by phone.

quote: When do you wanned to try to do it?
stewart_read: Customer volunteers to move to scheduling on his own initiative rather than being pushed there — a positive engagement signal the rep could have named back ('glad you're ready to get this locked in') before jumping straight into calendar options.
coaching_implication: Small miss, not a major gap: rep could briefly acknowledge the customer's own initiative to reinforce momentum, rather than immediately reciting time slots.

quote: I just saw that we had you on our calendar here, this just last Sunday to share that solar design that we built for your home. It just looks like that wasn't a good time.
stewart_read: The call reveals this is a second attempt at the same appointment; the rep does not investigate why the first one fell through (schedule conflict? customer avoidance? already decided on competitor by then?) before booking a second one with the same structural gaps (son absent).
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be intentionally not re-litigating the missed appointment to keep the call 'super quick' as promised — but this omits diagnostic information that would predict whether the second appointment also fails.
coaching_implication: When re-booking a previously missed appointment, ask one diagnostic question about what happened last time before re-committing calendar resources.

quote: if you'll if you could have that available to show to our specialist there, then we could kinda compare apples to apples
stewart_read: Rep correctly asks the customer to have the competitor's design available for comparison, matching the already_saw_design rebuttal strategy — but never asks what company it is or what the design showed, leaving the closer to start that discovery cold.
coaching_implication: Pair the 'bring the design' ask with a quick verbal capture of the competitor name and headline price/terms so the closer has it in the handoff.

quote: K. Awesome. Well, yeah, thank you for your time today, Wilbert, and we'll see you here tomorrow at 12PM noon.
stewart_read: Rep closes with a date/time confirmation but skips the full button-up protocol — no one-hour block statement, no 'is that fair?' handshake, no explicit text-follow-up promise, and no mention of the son needing to be present or informed.
coaching_implication: Drill the full button-up checklist so bookings on marginal leads like this one get the procedural reinforcement that improves show rate.
